glengoyne.name: Glengoyne
glengoyne.house_style: Slow-distilled, unpeated Highland single malt with a sherry-led signature: dried fruit, nutty oak and gentle spice, always bottled at natural colour and non-chill-filtered. The distillery prides itself on the slowest distillation in Scotland, capturing a clean, fruit-forward spirit; the recent White Oak / Oak Masters' series pivots the same spirit toward bright bourbon/virgin-oak vanilla-and-citrus territory.
glengoyne.notes: Sits on the Highland Line near Dumgoyne (stills in the Highlands, warehouses across the road in the Lowlands). Core range is sherry-led (12/15/18/21/25). The Oak Masters' Series (debut White Oak, 2024 UK / 2025 US) marks a deliberate 'new flavour direction' away from sherry toward American first-fill bourbon and virgin oak.

isle-of-skye.name: Isle of Skye (Ian Macleod blend)
isle-of-skye.house_style: A blended Scotch — NOT a single malt. Peated island malt (a Skye core, widely understood to lean on Talisker) softened by Speyside and Highland malts plus grain whisky; the house signature is gentle maritime smoke wrapped in honeyed orchard fruit, baking spice and oak rather than aggressive peat.
isle-of-skye.notes: Blend created in 1933 by a Skye-born blender named Ian Macleod from a 'secret family recipe', conceived as an homage to Clan Macleod (seat: Dunvegan Castle, Isle of Skye). The brand is owned by Ian Macleod Distillers (the company acquired it in 1963). Unusually deep core range spanning 8, 12, 18, 21, 25 and 30 Year Old. All expressions bottled at 40% ABV. The 25YO was named Best Blended Scotch Whisky in the World at the 2025 San Francisco World Spirits Competition; the 30YO took Gold at the 2026 World Whiskies Awards. IMPORTANT: 'Isle of Skye' the blend is distinct from the Talisker single malt distillery on Skye.

rosebank.name: Rosebank
rosebank.house_style: Delicate, floral, triple-distilled Lowland single malt — soft and intimate, with citrus, orchard fruit, grassy/herbal notes and a creamy, spirit-driven elegance. Long regarded as the benchmark of the Lowland style.
rosebank.notes: Lowland 'ghost' distillery, mothballed/closed 1993. Acquired by Ian Macleod Distillers in 2017; revived with a new distillery and visitor centre (production resumed July 2024, public reopening 2023-2024). The 'Legacy Series' of limited annual releases drew on casks laid down before closure: Release One = 30 Year Old (1990, bottled 2020, 48.6%); Release Two = 31 Year Old (1990/1991, bottled 2022, 48.1%); Release Three = 32 Year Old (2024). NOTE: a vintage conflict exists for the 31yo Release Two (sources state both 1990 and 1991) — see expression node rosebank-31-r2.

tamdhu.name: Tamdhu
tamdhu.house_style: 100% sherry-cask matured. Tamdhu is one of the few Speyside distilleries to mature its entire output exclusively in oloroso sherry-seasoned oak (first-fill and refill, European and American oak), sourced from bodegas in Jerez, Spain. The signature is a clean, unpeated, sherry-forward Speysider — dried fruit, nuts, dark chocolate and spice — frequently framed by critics as a value-driven alternative to The Macallan.
tamdhu.notes: Founded 1897 on the banks of the River Spey near Knockando. Owned by Ian Macleod Distillers since 2011. Core range built around sherry maturation (10, 12, 15, 18, and now 21 Year Old, plus Batch Strength). Founded year (1897) is from general/public knowledge and was NOT WebFetch-verified in this run (WebFetch returned HTTP 403 globally) — flag for verification.

bottles.display_name: Glengoyne 24 Year Old White Oak (Oak Masters' Series)
bottles.cask: American first-fill bourbon + virgin/new (white) oak. NOTE: distinct from the 25 Sherry Oak — the 24 White Oak is bourbon/virgin-oak matured (vanilla/citrus profile), NOT sherry. Debut release of the Oak Masters' Series.
bottles.outturn_or_availability: Limited release ('will not return once sold out'). UK launch 10 Jul 2024 (RRP £430); US debut Mar 2025 ($400). Exact outturn N/A — not found.

tasting.nose: Rich vanilla and toasted oak, lemon curd, honey, plum jam, desiccated coconut, spiced apple pastry dusted with icing sugar and lime zest; per Whisky Advocate also passion-fruit panna cotta, dried mango and cinnamon spice.
tasting.palate: Gently balanced and bright: lemon and key-lime pie, honeycomb, gentle tropical notes and soft oak, with star anise, vanilla and emerging chocolate (Whisky Advocate finds rich chocolate ganache/cocoa); Drinkhacker notes white chocolate, grapefruit pith and big toasty charred oak.
tasting.finish: Long and well-aged: toffee apple, delicate citrus and lingering oak, with chocolate sticking the landing.
tasting.narrative: This is Glengoyne off-script and the better for it. The slowest-distilled spirit in Scotland, normally dressed in sherry, is here pushed into American first-fill bourbon and virgin oak — and the result is bright, dessert-led and unmistakably NOT the 25. The nose is vanilla and toasted oak over lemon curd, honey, plum jam and desiccated coconut (Robb Report), with Whisky Advocate finding the more exotic register: passion-fruit panna cotta, dried mango and cinnamon. The palate is gently balanced — key-lime pie, honeycomb, soft tropical fruit and star anise — before chocolate muscles in: Whisky Advocate's ganache and cocoa, Drinkhacker's white chocolate over grapefruit pith and big charred oak. The finish is long and well-aged, toffee apple and citrus with cocoa sticking the landing. Pedigree is real: it was named among Robb Report's best whiskies of 2025 (their '10 Best Whiskeys of 2025 So Far', an unranked list — the earlier '#2' placement could not be confirmed on Robb Report's own site); Drinkhacker an A- (~90). My one reservation is Drinkhacker's, and it is fair — the spirit reads 'just now cresting into over-maturity', so the charred oak is loud. VERDICT: BUY and POUR, not collect — a genuinely accomplished citrus-and-vanilla 24yo at sane money (~£415 / $400), but the secondary tells you the market agrees this is a drinker: Whiskystats values it BELOW retail. No flipping upside. Keep its bright bourbon/virgin-oak profile strictly walled off from the 25 Sherry Oak.

bottles.cask: Exclusively sherry oak (hand-selected European/American sherry casks). NOTE: distinct from the 24 White Oak — the 25 is 100% sherry-matured. Some older labelling cites 'Oloroso Sherry Cask' — oloroso designation UNCONFIRMED for current standard 25.

tasting.nose: Dried figs and raisins, rich chocolate and toffee pudding, red fruits, leather and brown sugar.
tasting.palate: Warm oak, rich fig, raisins, decadent chocolate, hazelnut and butterscotch; soft oak, cinnamon, stewed fruits and a Seville-marmalade tang.
tasting.finish: Very long, spicy liquorice, slowly drying.
tasting.narrative: This is the orthodox Glengoyne: a quarter-century exclusively in hand-selected sherry casks, coppery-red in the glass and trading on depth rather than weight. The nose stacks dried figs, raisins, rich chocolate and toffee pudding over red fruits, leather and brown sugar; WhiskyNotes (Ruben Luyten) adds jammy juicy figs and soaked cherries, plums, blackberries, espresso and burnt sugar from first-fill European-oak sherry. The palate follows with warm oak, fig, raisins, decadent chocolate, hazelnut and butterscotch, lifted by cinnamon, stewed fruit and a Seville-marmalade tang (The Whiskey Wash; corroborated by the distillery's own notes); Drinkhacker finds it nutty and savoury — toasted walnuts, coconut husks, vanilla sponge, milk chocolate and a tannic, nougat-and-Christmas-spice finish. The finish is very long, spicy liquorice slowly drying out. Crucially for an old sherried malt, the captured notes show no sulphur and no sharpness — this is clean sherry maturation on Scotland's slowest-distilled spirit, natural colour and non-chill-filtered at 48%. Pedigree is real and now multiply-sourced: The Whiskey Wash named it Best Scotch at its 2025 Awards (its founder: 'Scotch whisky doesn't get any better than this', corroborated by Master of Malt's blog), Drinkhacker an A- (~90), and the Whiskybase crowd 89.74/100 across 324 ratings. VERDICT: POUR — a benchmark, textbook old-school sherried Highlander to drink, not to chase as an investment; UK retail runs ~£420 (Master of Malt) to £525 (Royal Mile), £499 at the distillery, while the secondary average (~£250) sits below it. Keep its dried-fruit/chocolate sherry profile firmly separate from the citrus-and-vanilla White Oak 24.

bottles.display_name: Isle of Skye 21 Year Old (Blended Scotch, Ian Macleod)
bottles.cask: Blend of peated island malts matched with Speyside and Highland malts plus grain whiskies. Specific cask regime N/A — not found (TWW notes 'Chestnut/Oloroso sherry' colour only).
bottles.outturn_or_availability: Ongoing core-range expression; not limited. 70cl. SRP US$114.99.

tasting.nose: Warm baking spices, red apples, buttery toffee, citrus and chocolate malted balls; a beautiful dry nuttiness with brown sugar, vanilla, cedar chest, nutmeg, cinnamon, dried citrus, coffee and walnut cake.
tasting.palate: Subtle stone-fruit sweetness — spicy caramel, blackcurrant, chocolate, lemon zest, a hint of cedar wood and green peppercorn; sweet and honeyed with hot oatmeal, chocolate sauce, strawberries, orange and a whirl of ground pepper and oak spice.
tasting.finish: Medium to long, deliciously rich and oaky, with a glimpse of peppermint.
tasting.narrative: The entry into Skye's older blends, and it behaves like one: a 40% island blend that leads with confection — buttery toffee, red apple, chocolate malted balls and warm baking spice — over a spine of dry, savoury nuttiness (Whisky Advocate's McCormick logs brown sugar, cedar chest, coffee and walnut cake; The Whiskey Wash adds spicy caramel, blackcurrant and a hint of green peppercorn). The palate is sweet and honeyed, with oatmeal, chocolate sauce, strawberry and orange before a whirl of ground pepper, then a medium-to-long, deliciously rich and oaky finish closed by a glimpse of peppermint. Two decades show as polish, not depth — TWW concedes it lands 'without an over abundance of complexity' even as it calls it 'a subtly decadent treat'; Whisky Magazine's Chris Neil, scoring it 8.6, reads it as a 'beautiful, mature whisky' with dusty coffee, juicy barley and a long, stony finish. The hardware agrees the make is clean: Tastings.com/BTI awarded 90 points and a Gold. VERDICT: POUR. A genuinely well-made, smooth aged blend at a sane ~£118/$115 — buy it to drink, not to be moved; the 25 is where the money should go.

bottles.display_name: Isle of Skye 25 Year Old (Blended Scotch, Ian Macleod)
bottles.cask: Mature whiskies from Skye and mainland Scotland; high malt content; matured in ex-bourbon and sherry casks (per The Whiskey Wash). Blend leans on a Talisker core plus Speyside and Lowland whiskies (per Whisky Advocate).
bottles.outturn_or_availability: Ongoing premium core-range expression; not limited. 70cl. SRP US$179 / £250.

tasting.nose: Rich oak, ginger, vanilla, red apple and citrus; earthy autumn leaves, warm baking spices, brown sugar, orchard fruits, toasted walnuts, burnt-orange citrus and buttery toffee. (TWE: Comice pear and apricot.)
tasting.palate: Rounded and fruity — malt, apple and light peat smoke; with complexity of hazelnuts, warm spices, blood-orange zest, dark wood polish, gentle smoke, a touch of sea salt and a spot of leather. Whisky Advocate notes cola, allspice, red apple, liquorice, leather, gingerbread, clove, black tea, peaty embers, dark toffee and milk chocolate.
tasting.finish: Long and balanced with subtle apricot; long and smoky (TWE).
tasting.narrative: The flagship, and the one expression here that earns its hype. A high-malt blend of Skye and mainland whiskies pulled from ex-bourbon and sherry casks, with a Talisker core supplying the gentle maritime smoke. The nose is autumnal and layered — rich oak, ginger, vanilla, red apple and burnt-orange citrus over toasted walnut and buttery toffee, with Comice pear and apricot per The Whisky Exchange. The palate is rounded and genuinely complex: malt and apple lift into hazelnut, blood-orange zest, dark wood polish, a touch of sea salt and leather, with Whisky Advocate cataloguing cola, allspice, liquorice, gingerbread, clove, black tea, peaty embers, dark toffee and milk chocolate. The finish runs long, balanced and faintly smoky with subtle apricot. The hardware backs the glass: Whisky Advocate's McCormick scored it 94 and called it 'a 25 year old that offers great value,' Wine Enthusiast's Kara Newman went higher at 97 ('a rich and inviting sip' of caramel, cocoa, toffee and fresh-roasted coffee closing on orange marmalade and crushed hazelnut), and SFWSC 2025 named it Best Blended Scotch (16+) AND Best Overall Blended Scotch Whisky (announced 12 Nov 2025, Edinburgh, blind, 1,500+ entries), judges calling it 'a beautifully crafted Scotch.' VERDICT: BUY. The standout of the line and a benchmark aged blend at ~£250/$179-210; the strength is the only thing holding it back from being unarguable.

bottles.display_name: Isle of Skye 30 Year Old (Blended Scotch, Ian Macleod)
bottles.cask: Malt and grain whiskies aged at least 30 years, married in oak; single malt from the Scottish islands, Speyside and Highlands matured in a selection of oak casks. Talisker forms the smoky maritime core.
bottles.outturn_or_availability: Rare top-of-range expression; ongoing but low volume. 70cl. SRP ~US$322 / £299.

tasting.nose: Lush, earthy 'forest floor after rain' notes with fragrant red berries, cinnamon, citrus, buttery caramel and salted pretzels; citrus peel, pepper, Madagascan vanilla pods, marzipan, cigar smoke and a hint of cherry.
tasting.palate: Vivid and complex — warm spices, black tea, lemon citrus, vanilla, orchard fruits and brown sugar, with hints of soft leather and chocolate malted balls; soft and sweet with heather honey, baked orange, tobacco smoke, clove, raisin, Brazil nut, walnut oil, toasted sesame and coffee cake.
tasting.finish: Long and mellow; soft peat, dried fruit, vanilla and malted biscuit lingering — complex without being heavy.
tasting.narrative: The summit of the range, and it drinks like a decanted afternoon. The nose is lush and earthy — The Whiskey Wash's 'forest floor after it rains' — with fragrant red berries, cinnamon, citrus, buttery caramel and salted pretzels; Whisky Advocate layers in citrus peel, pepper, Madagascan vanilla pods, marzipan, cigar smoke and a hint of cherry. The palate is vivid and complex: warm spice, black tea, lemon, vanilla and orchard fruit over brown sugar, soft leather and chocolate malted balls, deepening into heather honey, baked orange, tobacco smoke, clove, raisin, Brazil nut, walnut oil and coffee cake. The finish is long and mellow — soft peat, dried fruit, vanilla and malted biscuit — complex without being heavy. WA's McCormick frames it as 'an indulgent blend for swirling around the glass or pairing with a cigar,' The Whiskey Reviewer grades it A- ('marvelous' palate of butter pastry, fresh malt and raisin, though the finish fades to 'a non-entity'), and Drinkhacker folds it into a favourable complete-lineup review; the medals agree, with Gold at the 2026 World Whiskies Awards for depth, subtlety and balance, plus IWSC Spirit Gold and SFWSC Gold cited at retail. VERDICT: POUR — buy for the occasion, not the everyday. Genuinely complex and beautifully aged, but at ~£299/$330 the 40% ABV caps the intensity, and the better value still sits one rung down at the 25.

bottles.cask: 62% refill sherry butts & 38% refill bourbon hogsheads
bottles.identity_note: ORCHESTRATOR SLUG CAVEAT: this node uses the assigned slug 'rosebank-31-r1', but Rosebank's Legacy Release One is a 30 YEAR OLD (1990, bottled 2020, 48.6% ABV), NOT a 31 Year Old. The 31 Year Old is Release Two (rosebank-31-r2). age_years and abv here reflect the true Release One bottle.

tasting.nose: Buttery and golden: rich vanilla, lemon meringue pie, honeycomb, polished oak, marzipan and a pinch of wood spice; vibrant citrus with orange zest, watermelon, apple skin, peach and nectarine; Chantilly cream and caramel wafers.
tasting.palate: Creamy, buttery and fruity with a gentle spiciness; sweet almonds, butterscotch, grapefruit peel, gooseberry, chamomile, pears and pineapple.
tasting.finish: Soft and intimate, with pear and vanilla; background wood spice.
tasting.narrative: Identity first, because the label invites confusion: this is the Legacy Release ONE, a 30 Year Old (1990, bottled 2020, 48.6%) — not the 31yo (that is Release Two). What is in the glass is textbook delicate triple-distilled Lowland: spirit-driven, soft and intimate rather than oak-led, the refill sherry/bourbon casks framing the fruit instead of smothering it. The nose is buttery and golden — Whisky Advocate's Jonny McCormick logs vanilla, lemon meringue pie, honeycomb, marzipan and polished oak, while Words of Whisky widens it into vibrant citrus, watermelon, peach and nectarine. The palate stays creamy and fruity with a gentle spice (sweet almonds, butterscotch, grapefruit peel, gooseberry), closing soft on pear and vanilla. Connosr's markjedi1 was unguarded — 'the nose is just out of this world' — and Whisky Advocate's 92 points confirms the pedigree. VERDICT: a benchmark Lowland and a blue-chip collectible, but the maths is sober — at £2k+ secondary against a £1,600 RRP you are paying a heavy ghost-distillery premium for poise, not power. Collect it; don't expect a bargain pour.

bottles.vintage_conflict_note: VINTAGE CONFLICT (preserved & flagged): Whisky Auctioneer bottle hub and Whiskyhunter state distilled 1990; Whisky Auctioneer product listing 1280618 is titled 'Rosebank 1991 31 Year Old Release #2' and Whiskybase carries alt slug 'rosebank-1991'. Both 1990 and 1991 are reported in sources; unresolved. Age (31yo) and bottling year (2022) are consistent across sources.

tasting.nose: Champagne gold. Banana cake, cherry blossom and lavender with malt and virgin oak shavings; baked apple, peach and apple butter over a grassy/herbaceous backbone; nutty, mossy, furniture polish giving way to floral elderflower and lemon with a light briny edge.
tasting.palate: Velvety soft dried grass reminiscent of chamomile tea; wild strawberries and sweet lemon citrus over toasted marshmallow; toffee, glazed nuts, vanilla cream, baked apple, citrus and a little cocoa; tea leaf, sandalwood, vanilla cookies and baking spice, with modest oak tannin.
tasting.finish: Bubbly champagne and oak with a slight medicinal flavour; well-balanced, with a roasty edge balancing the sweetness.
tasting.narrative: This is the headline bottle — the Legacy Release TWO, the genuine 31 Year Old (bottled 2022, 48.1%), as distinct from the 30yo Release One. It is the delicate triple-distilled Lowland ideal in full: champagne-gold, floral and grassy, more reticent on the nose than in the mouth. The Whiskey Wash finds banana cake, cherry blossom, lavender and virgin oak shavings; Words of Whisky reads it as nutty and mossy with furniture polish washed away by elderflower and lemon over a light briny edge. The palate is where it speaks up — Paste Magazine and The Whiskey Wash converge on velvety dried-grass chamomile, wild strawberry and sweet lemon citrus over toasted marshmallow, then toffee, glazed nuts, vanilla cream and a little cocoa, the oak adding only modest tannin and a roasty edge that checks the sweetness. Words of Whisky's verdict stands: 'an ideal of what traditional Lowland whisky is.' Scores back it (Whisky Auctioneer 91, Whiskybase 90.42), and it carries competition metal. One caveat for the record: sources disagree on vintage (1990 vs 1991 — see vintage_conflict_note); age and 2022 bottling are consistent. VERDICT: an excellent, poised Lowland keeper that rewards patience over power — collect it, but go in clear-eyed that the £2k-plus collector premium buys provenance, not value.

bottles.display_name: Tamdhu 18 Year Old (Oloroso Sherry Cask Matured)
bottles.cask: Exclusively oloroso sherry-seasoned casks — combination of European and American oak, sourced from Jerez, Spain
bottles.outturn_or_availability: Limited release / core range (annual). Exact outturn N/A — not found

tasting.nose: Dry nutty sherry, cherry and plum, milk chocolate, rum raisin, citrus and baked/honeyed oats; orange zest and hazelnut milk chocolate (per retailer notes).
tasting.palate: Rich, complex and decadently sherried — vanilla, brown sugar, red apple and dried fruits, deep nutty richness, dark chocolate and toasted almonds, with a characteristic dryness.
tasting.finish: N/A — not found (no critic finish text exposed in the captured excerpts).
tasting.narrative: NOSE: dry, nutty oloroso — cherry and plum, milk chocolate and rum raisin, lifted by citrus and baked/honeyed oats; the retailer adds orange zest and hazelnut milk chocolate (Whiskey Wash, TWE). PALATE: rich and decadently sherried — vanilla, brown sugar, red apple and dried fruit over deep nutty richness, dark chocolate and toasted almonds, all carried on a characteristic dryness (Whiskey Wash). FINISH: not captured. This is Tamdhu's full-throttle oloroso statement at 46.8%, natural colour and un-chill-filtered, matured exclusively in European/American-oak sherry casks from Jerez. Whiskey Wash calls it 'a sherry bomb whisky at the height of its greatness'; it took a Double Gold at the San Francisco World Spirits Competition. VERDICT: a benchmark dry-sherried Speysider and a credible value play against Macallan at ~$200 — buy to drink. bottles.display_name: Tamdhu 21 Year Old (Oloroso Sherry Cask Matured)
bottles.cask: Exclusively Oloroso sherry-seasoned casks — hand-selected combination of first-fill & refill American and European oak (European oak dominant), sourced from Jerez, Spain
bottles.outturn_or_availability: Core range (oldest core-range expression). 12,000 bottles worldwide; global release Aug 2025, arrived in US market Aug 2025.

tasting.nose: Wisps of sherried oak with chocolate, sultanas and warm cinnamon porridge; plump raisins and fresh figs, red berries and orange peels, whiffs of old oak and a hint of furniture wax, tobacco leaves and walnut skins, toffee and cinnamon syrup (official + WhiskyNotes/Whiskey Wash).
tasting.palate: Christmas cake of plump raisins, candied orange and gentle oak. A sweet spot between European oak spice and the roundness of American oak — creamy, juicy mouthfeel with bold dense flavours: bitter dark chocolate, cocoa nibs and bittersweet coffee, then sweet vanilla pods, fresh ground clove and nutmeg, dried sultanas and raisins tempered by fresher red grapefruit, orange zest and a tropical kumquat twist.
tasting.finish: Endless waves of oak and spice that finally give way to sweet fruit; glides between rich oak, intense Christmas fruits and spices and refreshing ginger and citrus.
tasting.narrative: NOSE: sherried oak with chocolate, sultanas and warm cinnamon porridge (official), opening to plump raisins and fresh figs, red berries and orange peel, with old oak, a hint of furniture wax, tobacco leaf and walnut skin, toffee and cinnamon syrup over a fresh, heady character (WhiskyNotes, Whiskey Wash). PALATE: a Christmas cake of plump raisins, candied orange and gentle oak — the critics agree on a 'sweet spot' between European-oak spice and American-oak roundness; creamy and juicy, with bold, dense flavours of bitter dark chocolate, cocoa nibs and bittersweet coffee, then sweet vanilla pods, clove and nutmeg, dried sultanas and raisins lifted by red grapefruit, orange zest and a tropical kumquat twist (WhiskyNotes, Whiskey Wash, Whisky For Everyone). FINISH: long — waves of rich oak, intense Christmas fruit and spice that give way to refreshing ginger and citrus. This is Tamdhu's oldest standing expression and its most decorated: Overall Winner at the 2026 Spirit of Speyside Whisky Awards (Gold, 18-and-over) and Whisky of the Year at the Scottish Field Whisky Challenge. Matured exclusively in hand-selected first-fill and refill American and European oak oloroso from Jerez, European oak dominant, at 47.5%, natural colour, un-chill-filtered. The value case is the headline: Robb Report's Jonah Flicker calls it a 'decadent sherry bomb for Macallan lovers,' just four years younger than the Macallan 25 yet ~$400 against the Macallan's ~$3,000 — 'just as good, if not better'; WhiskyNotes judges the oak balance 'just right ... not outrageously priced.' VERDICT: buy and open it. A genuinely accomplished, fairly-priced sherried Speysider that earns its awards and its Macallan-alternative billing. Caveats for the record: no numeric /100 score was confirmed (Robb Report only implies the 85-89 'Very Good' band), all captures are WebSearch-surfaced (WebFetch 403), and at one year old it has no secondary-market track record.
